content:
Stephanie Nguyen: Dropping here for sales leadership review before we lock v1 routing + suppression. Goal is: high-signal triggers only, clean ownership, no duplicate outreach.

Proposed v1 routing (from Sales Ops draft):
- If company country in US/CA -> NA queue (Stephanie)
- If in EU/UK/CH/NO/SE/DK/NL/BE/FR/DE/ES/IT/IE -> EMEA queue (Lukas)
- Else -> “ROW” queue (we’ll manually assign in pilot)

Segmentation:
- Self-serve + <$5k/mo = SDR-led first touch, AE added only if meetings booked
- >=$5k/mo OR “security intent” signal = AE-owned task created immediately, SDR assists if needed

Suppression:
- If Active Deal exists in HubSpot (any stage past Discovery) -> suppress signal tasks
- If Enterprise account managed by CS (tag) -> suppress SDR sequence; notify CSM + owning AE

SLA expectations:
- “High intent” (security questionnaire/doc clicks + pricing visits) -> first touch within 4 biz hours
- “Usage pain” (429s/latency/rate-limit hits) -> 1 biz day

Can folks poke holes / confirm we can live with this for pilot?

Isabelle Laurent: +1 on keeping it simple for v1. A couple clarifications:
1) “Active Deal exists” needs an exact definition or we’ll miss coverage. In HubSpot we can check `num_open_deals` and/or deal stage != Closed Won/Lost. I’d propose: suppress only if there’s an OPEN deal associated with the company.
2) We should still log the signal to the timeline even if suppressed, so AEs can see it later.

Lukas Meyer: For EMEA routing, country list is fine, but we also need to account for residency intent. We’ve got a bunch of US-inc companies with “must run in eu-west” requirements. If the signal includes `region_residency = EU`, I want those to route to my team regardless of HQ.

Stephanie Nguyen: Good call. That’s one of the signals we’re adding (region/residency constraints). We can override geo if they explicitly indicate EU data residency.

David Kim: From HubSpot side, we can implement the override as workflow logic:
- If `plg_region_residency` contains “EU” -> assign to EMEA owner (Lukas’ rules)
- Else do country-based assignment

Also agree w/ Isabelle: suppression should prevent TASK/SEQUENCE enrollment but still write a timeline event like “PLG Signal (Suppressed): reason=Open Deal”.

Grace O'Connor: SDR SLA: 4 biz hours for “high intent” might be tight if it fires overnight or weekend. Suggest:
- “within 4 biz hours” during business days
- “by noon local time next business day” if fired after hours

Otherwise we’ll start missing our own SLA and it’ll look bad in reporting.

Jordan Blake: We’re not trying to create a new pager here. I want speed, but realistic. Grace’s suggestion works.

Also: make sure suppression avoids embarrassing double-touches. If an AE is already in convo, SDR shouldn’t blast a sequence because someone hit the pricing page 3x.

Isabelle Laurent: +100. I’d like an additional suppression check:
- If last outbound email logged in HubSpot within 7 days -> don’t enroll sequence, just create a low-priority task/note.

We can keep “cool-down” as 14 days for the same signal type.

Markus Klein: From SE side: can we add a lightweight tag when it’s “Dedicated-fit” vs “Private-fit”? Helps us triage handoffs.
E.g., signal types:
- sustained spend + concurrency spikes -> “Dedicated likely”
- security intent + residency -> “Private likely”

Not asking for perfection, just a nudge.

Stephanie Nguyen: That’s in the scoring spec as “recommended_offer”. We can expose it in the Slack notif + HubSpot timeline copy. (We should avoid it being too prescriptive though.)

Jasmine Liu: CS suppression: please don’t send SDR sequences to accounts tagged as “Enterprise - CSM Managed” even if no open deal. It causes confusion because they’re already in quarterly check-ins.

Instead:
- timeline event for visibility
- Slack notify #customer-success (or create a CS task) when it’s a clear expansion signal (spend up, repeated 429s)

David Kim: We can implement that with a property like `cs_managed_account=true` (already exists as “CS Managed Tier”). If true:
- do NOT enroll SDR sequence
- create a task assigned to the CSM (Jasmine’s team) OR post to #customer-success (if we go that route)

Stephanie Nguyen: Great. For sales leadership review, here are the updated proposals based on this thread:

Routing v1:
- Override: `region_residency=EU` -> EMEA owner
- Else route by company country: NA vs EMEA vs ROW queue

Suppression v1:
- If OPEN deal exists -> suppress tasks/sequences; still write timeline event w/ reason
- If CS managed enterprise -> suppress SDR sequence; notify CSM/AE; still timeline event
- Cool-down: 14 days per (company, signal_type)
- Optional: if outbound activity in last 7 days -> no sequence, task only (Isabelle to confirm feasibility)

SLA v1:
- High intent: 4 biz hours during business day; otherwise by noon local next business day
- Usage pain: 1 biz day

Any objections before we tell Logan/Nadia to lock this into the workflow config?

Lukas Meyer: No objections. Please make sure “ROW queue” doesn’t silently die. Even if manual, we should have a weekly review / reassignment.

Isabelle Laurent: No objections. The “outbound in last 7 days” rule is feasible but depends on consistent activity logging. For pilot: I’d implement as best-effort + include in reporting as “attempted suppression”.

Grace O'Connor: Works for SDR. I’ll update the pilot expectations doc w/ the SLA wording and how to log outcomes.

Jordan Blake: Approved for pilot. Keep the lead volume manageable. If we see spammy behavior (false positives), we tighten fast.

(reaction :thumbsup: from Stephanie Nguyen)

David Kim: I’ll update the HubSpot workflow draft with:
- suppression reasons enum
- override routing rule for EU residency
- timeline event write even on suppression

Will post screenshots in #help once it’s in sandbox.

Jasmine Liu: Thanks. Please also add “CS suppression reason” text so we can audit why something didn’t route to SDR.

Stephanie Nguyen: Noted. I’ll sync this summary to the PRD comments and tag Product Ops.
